items.title: Minnesota Just Sent A Somali Daycare Owner To The Statehouse - Wait Till You See The Money
items.summary: Minnesota Just Sent A Somali Daycare Owner To The Statehouse - Wait Till You See The Money Minnesota voters on Tuesday elected a Somali daycare owner whose center has collected $7.29 million from the state childcare subsidy program at the heart of last winter's viral fraud scandal. Abdi Daisane was elected to represent the St. Cloud area in the Minnesota House. (Abdi Daisane for State Representative) / (Peter D'Abrosca/Fox News Digital) Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) candidate Abdi Daisane, a ...

scraped.title: Minnesota Just Sent A Somali Daycare Owner To The Statehouse - Wait Till You See The Money
scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: Minnesota Just Sent A Somali Daycare Owner To The Statehouse - Wait Till You See The Money
scraped.body_text:
Minnesota voters on Tuesday elected a Somali daycare owner whose center has collected $7.29 million from the state childcare subsidy program at the heart of last winter's viral fraud scandal.

Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) candidate Abdi Daisane, a Somali American who came to the US more than 15 years ago, won House District 14A with about 52% of the vote, beating Republican Mike Conway, the St. Cloud City Council president, and flipping a Republican-held seat, MPR News reported . He becomes St. Cloud's first Somali American state lawmaker. Daisane lost the same race in 2024 to Republican Rep. Bernie Perryman, who ran for the state Senate this year instead.

Daisane gave part of his victory speech in Somali.

He spoke Somali for his victory speech https://t.co/6P67kFelZT pic.twitter.com/9xxZyj3Wnd

— End Wokeness (@EndWokeness) November 4, 2026

Daisane launched his second run for the seat on Christmas Eve 2025, the New York Post reported at the time. Two days later, YouTuber Nick Shirley posted his video tour of seemingly empty Somali-linked daycares - drawing more than 131 million views on X in five days, and FBI Director Kash Patel said the bureau had surged agents and resources to Minnesota as the Trump administration froze childcare funding to the state. Days before Tuesday's election, the Justice Department uncovered another $29 million in Minnesota benefits fraud.

Daisane hasn't been charged with anything, and we found no sign his center appeared in Shirley's videos.

Daisane is the CEO of Blooming Kids Child Care Center in St. Cloud. The center received $7.29 million in Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP) payments from 2018 through 2025, according to Department of Children, Youth, and Families data posted by the Minnesota House's Fraud Prevention and State Agency Oversight Committee. The payments more than tripled in three years, from $439,034 in 2021 to $1.54 million in 2024 , and held at $1.52 million in 2025. DCYF, which runs CCAP, wouldn't provide payment information when Alpha News asked.

Blooming Kids also took in $598,251.62 in approved claims from the federally funded Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) since late 2020, according to Minnesota Department of Education records Alpha News obtained through a data request. MDE hadn't confirmed the figure as of Alpha's report.

From 2020 into early 2022, the center's CACFP sponsor was Partners in Nutrition, Department of Education records reviewed by Alpha News show. In September, Partners in Nutrition agreed to hand over $18.5 million, everything it had, and permanently dissolve to settle Attorney General Keith Ellison's lawsuit alleging it knowingly and repeatedly billed the state for meals that were never served between October 2020 and February 2022, and facilitated widespread fraud at the sites it was supposed to be monitoring.

Ellison put PIN in the same breath as Feeding Our Future , the nonprofit at the center of Minnesota's pandemic food-aid fraud prosecutions, blaming "bad actors like PIN and Feeding Our Future" for eroding trust in government programs. "My office continues to actively investigate a number of individuals and entities affiliated with PIN for violations of the Minnesota False Claims Act," he said. Blooming Kids was not among the food sites named in the lawsuit. Alpha News asked whether the center, Daisane or anyone tied to it had been investigated in connection with Partners in Nutrition; Ellison's office didn't respond.

Late last month, a worker at a nearby business told Alpha News, " I do not recall ever seeing children entering or leaving the facility, " and said a white van tied to the center carried only an adult driver. The same source later reported seeing roughly 5 to 10 school-age children on the rear playground around 5:00 to 5:30 p.m. on some occasions. Fox News Digital visited on Thursday and found a mostly empty parking lot, windows covered in tinted, mirrored film and a paper sign on the front door directing visitors to another entrance.

State regulators have cited Blooming Kids for at least 16 licensing violations in three reviews between October 2024 and October 2025 , Alpha News found in state records. In the October 2024 review, regulators found children "were subjected to prohibited disciplinary actions." An April 2025 licensing investigation found staff "did not supervise the children at all times." The October 2025 review flagged infants not placed on their backs to sleep without the required documentation, unlabeled infant bottles and lapses in required CPR and first-aid training.

The state also fined the center $400 in November 2024 for two background-study violations, including letting an employee work for nearly seven months after the worker's background study expired. The order was addressed to Daisane as the center's authorized agent. The Department of Human Services' licensing database shows another review, on Oct. 8 of this year, that also found violations. Blooming Kids is licensed for up to 113 children, and its license remains active.

During his first run in 2024, after a 2023 review cited the center for equipment in disrepair and missing immunization and staff-qualification records, Daisane told St. Cloud Live, "I have always prioritized providing a safe and nurturing environment for all children," and said that when problems come up, "we learn from our mistakes and we do better next time."

Daisane's wife told BBC Somali in 2023 that she crossed the US-Mexico border to join him , an interview that resurfaced online during the campaign. "I smuggled myself and jumped over the wall for my love," she said, according to Alpha News' translation .

scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: Microsoft Pulls The Plug On Oracle AI Rental As Post-Election Data Center Fallout Spreads
scraped.body_text:
More bad news for Oracle.

About an hour after we checked in with Oracle's PR team on how that whole " force majeure is commonplace" thing was working out...

Hey guys, any updates here? https://t.co/GCPReT2mE1

... we got our answer, just not from Oracle :

Guess not: *MICROSOFT IS WINDING DOWN ORACLE DEAL TO RENT AI CLOUD CAPACITY https://t.co/2MizsjS9yq

According to Bloomberg , Microsoft has spent recent months switching off the computing capacity it rented from Oracle after declining to renew the contract. The reason is about as unflattering as it gets for a company that has staked its balance sheet on AI infrastructure: the Oracle hardware ran on older-generation Nvidia chips and, over time, "no longer fit the company's specifications."

ORCL promptly slid 4%, which put it, in our words, below the $116 equity offering price it sold $10 billion in stock at just four days ago. Recall that the stock hit $248.15 on June 1. Investors who bought the "de-risked" story this week are already underwater on a deal that is barely four days old , and the stock has lost more than half its value in five months.

But the Microsoft headline is just the latest entry on a list that has grown every single day since Tuesday night, when voters handed governors' mansions in the states holding roughly 45% of planned US data center capacity to candidates who promised to pause them. Put the two together and Oracle has a problem at both ends of its pipeline: its old capacity is too old to rent , and its new capacity may be too blue to build .

Some history first. The Oracle-Microsoft deal was announced in 2023 to power the AI version of Bing, and at the time, Bloomberg notes, the idea of Microsoft renting servers from a direct rival was taken as early proof of just how short the world was of compute. (The full size of the deal was never disclosed.)

Three years later, the same arrangement is proof of something else: GPUs age, and the biggest buyer of rented compute in the world is no longer willing to pay for the old ones.

Oracle, naturally, disagrees. A spokesperson told Bloomberg demand for its AI infrastructure "remains strong, including for earlier-generation" GPUs, and reminded everyone that in September it said it was renewing contracts for four-year-old GPUs at a 20% premium to the original price. That 20% premium has been a staple of the bull case: just this Wednesday, Wells Fargo's Jerry Revich, in " Texas Policy Reset Adds Timing Risk to 20-30% of the Data Center Power Pipeline " ( available to pro subs ), cited Oracle's 97.9% AI infrastructure utilization and "20% average renewal/resale premium" as evidence that "token economics remain attractive."

Well, one renewal just came in at a 100% discount.

Microsoft's retreat also fits a pattern we have been tracking for weeks. Microsoft committed more than $80 billion to rent capacity from neoclouds like CoreWeave, Nscale and Nebius, and per Bloomberg, key leaders there have grown frustrated over high costs and delays, tightened oversight of data center projects and debated whether to sign any new neocloud deals at all. In October, Microsoft walked from Nscale's UK deal ; on Thursday came the report that it won't expand its Texas deal with Nscale either , along with the disclosure that it spent $5 billion less on Q3 capex than projected due to delays at third-party capacity, including IREN's.

Translation: Microsoft wants new chips, on time, in its own specifications, and it is increasingly unwilling to pay landlords who can't deliver all three. Which is a problem for every landlord whose collateral is a rack of chips that gets one generation older every year the power doesn't show up.

And the power is now even less likely to show up on time.

Cleanview counts nine states where the governor or governor-elect has promised or already imposed a pause on new data centers. Together they hold 158.6 GW of planned capacity, or 41% of the entire US pipeline :

Now look at who is most exposed. Every single gigawatt of OpenAI's planned capacity sits in a state whose new governor backed a pause on the campaign trail , as does 45% of Microsoft's:

Why does that matter for Oracle? Because OpenAI is Oracle. The $300 billion compute contract that sent ORCL soaring in September 2025 is being built across Texas (Abilene, Shackelford County), New Mexico, Wisconsin and Michigan, which is why OpenAI shows up at 100% above. Two of those states, Texas and New Mexico, delivered the most hostile results of the night.

Take New Mexico, home of Project Jupiter, the 2.45 GW Oracle-OpenAI Stargate campus that regular readers know all too well. Back on Sept 24 Oracle sent a force majeure notice to the Blue Owl unit developing the site, then insisted the notice was "commonplace" and meant nothing. We had a different reading at the time:

Hey guys, you are right: the force majeure by itself does not change delivery expectations. You just have to pay the rent until the delivery actually takes place. Contractually. https://t.co/GCPReT1OOt pic.twitter.com/rj721cRTu9

The more important detail came that night, when the FT reported that Oracle remains on the contractual hook regardless: if Jupiter isn't ready, Oracle still owes a "carry cost" in lieu of rent for up to three years, enough to cover the interest on the debt in full plus a set equity return for Blue Owl's funds. As one person familiar with the contract put it, "The power delivery risk sits with Oracle, not the investors." Here is the structure we mapped out at the time. Note who sits at the bottom of every arrow:

And for the record, here is what we wrote in that same Sept 24 post , six weeks before the vote: the construction delays "will only get worse if Democrats win back the house at the midterm elections." They won back a lot more than the House, so we'll allow ourselves a modest victory lap.

Two weeks later, Oracle was trucking compressed natural gas to its data centers because the Jupiter pipeline was running late, and the $18 billion of construction loans behind the campus were already quoted at 89-91 cents on the dollar (per the FT).

On Tuesday, New Mexico elected Deb Haaland, and the morning after, she told reporters her plan for day one : "a moratorium for large-scale data centers with the legislature passing a set of guardrails." As for Jupiter's gas plants specifically, Cleanview notes Haaland has written that under her watch they would "not exist." The fuel-cell air permit is still pending, with a Nov 23 decision deadline. Hey guys, any updates?

Texas is no better. As we laid out in " What's Next For Data Centers After The Blue Tsunami ", governor-elect Gina Hinojosa turns Abbott's audit-based freeze into one tied to legislation, which means at least through the May 31, 2027 session end. And the Goldman TMT desk noted this morning that part of today's bounce came from "benign comments from Texas governor-elect on datacenters." When "benign" is the bull catalyst, you know where the bar is.

Goldman's research department spent Friday pushing back on the panic, and in fairness, it has the numbers. In his " End of Week Market Intelligence: dc downside ?" ( available to pro subs ), Chris Hussey frames this week's debate as follows:

"At the core of market concerns this week is a debate around whether all of the compute power that has been ordered (semiconductors, servers, fiber optic cables) will have a place to be installed when it is delivered in the years ahead ."

Goldman's answer is mostly yes, at least through 2027. Hardware analyst Mike Ng " US Data Center Capacity update: Framing risks to our data center forecasts ", also available to pro subs) says capacity already under construction implies 22/24 GW-IT of net additions in 2027/28, matching his 20/24 GW forecasts, and calls the key risk "timing rather than cancellations." The catch is Texas, which accounts for 20% of 2027 and 27% of 2028 under-construction additions:

E&C analyst Adam Bubes went a step further and actually raised his US data center construction spending forecasts to $80 billion/$100 billion for 2026/27 (from $67 billion/$87 billion), introducing $125 billion for 2028. His reasoning: every project in Goldman's 2027 forecast has already broken ground. 2028 is another story, though: only about half of the 2028 projects on Goldman's watch list have broken ground , and beyond that it's almost all PowerPoint:

Note the light blue. That is the "announced" capacity, and it is exactly what a governor's moratorium hits first. Bubes concedes as much, arguing moratoria "would primarily impact projects that have not yet started" and would smooth the cycle into 2029/30 "rather than impacting the TAM."

Maybe. But today's Microsoft story shows why "timing" is not as harmless as it sounds. A project that slips two years gets delivered into a world where the chips ordered for it are two years older. For a hyperscaler, a delay is a timing issue. For whoever owns the GPUs, it's a depreciation issue. Microsoft just told Oracle which one it is.

And somebody is going to have to fund the wait. Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam estimates hyperscalers are financing 36% of this year's capex with credit (and 35% next year), while only 43% of the $687 billion of AI-related financing so far this year came from hyperscalers. Oracle has already done its share: as we noted on Monday, it blew through its entire four-year $20 billion "hard cap" in a single morning, five days after promising it. Which, as regular readers know, is why we have been calling AI a debt bubble since last October.

The Oracle news landed at the end of a week that saw the Nasdaq suffer its worst day since March 2020 on Thursday (-6.4%), while Goldman's AI data center-levered basket fell 12% in a single session. The headlines since then haven't helped much:

Here is the updated ZH Casualty List , with Oracle as the newest entry:

Jefferies' Julien Dumoulin-Smith summed up the sellside consensus on the election in one line " The Blue Morning After: State-by-State Election Scorecard "): "Demand moves right, not away." Goldman says the same thing with more charts.

Perhaps they're right about demand. But capacity that moves right ages , financing that moves right costs more , and a landlord that moves right keeps paying for the slip (just ask Oracle's lenders on Jupiter). Today's Microsoft story is the first clear sign of what happens at the other end: the tenant with the deepest pockets in AI is choosing newer chips over older contracts , and that probably makes Oracle's 20% renewal premium look a lot more like an exception.

Which leaves Oracle squeezed on both sides: the older chips it already owns are losing their best renter, while the new campuses meant to replace them sit in exactly the states that just voted for a pause. Goldman hosted Oracle management today, of all days; we'd love to know what was said in the room. Until then, we'll keep asking the obvious question:

If Oracle has cash flow visibility all the way to 2029 maybe they can answer something far simpler: when will the force majeure on their massive NM data center be lifted? What’s that, they have no idea?

Much more in the full Goldman " End of Week Market Intelligence: dc downside ?", and " US Data Center Capacity update " both available to pro subs .

Robert Inlakesh analyses the outcome of the Israeli election, what it means and provides the context to the racist rhetoric, in addition to physical attacks on Palestinian voters, in this Thursday’s Target Stream.

scraped.body_text:
A new Democrat-led House Committee on the Judiciary report released this week sheds more light on President Donald Trump’s close relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. The Document, entitled “‘We Have Certain Things in Common, Jeffrey’: The Case Against Donald Trump Emerging in the Epstein Files and DOJ’s Desperate Efforts to Cover it Up,” is based on the accounts of eleven women, five of whom alleged Trump raped or sexually assaulted them in the presence of the disgraced financier. Two of those women were 13-year-old children at the time of the alleged events.

The report portrays both Trump and former United States Special Representative for Global Partnerships Paolo Zampolli as being members of Epstein’s trafficking inner circle, and catalogs how Trump’s Department of Justice (DOJ) “actively obstructed the Epstein investigation into any co-conspirators” and attempted to block the release of the Epstein Files in order to protect the president.

Even so, Trump’s name still appears roughly 38,000 times in the released Epstein Files, with Epstein himself claiming that he introduced Trump’s future wife Melania to him, and that the pair first had sex aboard his infamous “Lolita Express” jet. Melania was, at the time, a model working for Zampolli’s agency.

Beatrice Keul – In 1993, Miss Switzerland Beatrice Keul was in New York City competing in Trump’s American Dream Pageant. It was there that she met both the future president and Jeffrey Epstein. Trump offered to secure her a place at New York University, and for Zampolli to arrange her visa. Epstein, she said, described himself as “Don’s best friend.”

Keul went to a suite in the Plaza Hotel for what she thought was a meeting about NYU. However, upon entering the suite, she said, Trump grabbed her from behind and “brutally” raped her, tearing her dress and caused bleeding and bruising across her body.

“ Katie Johnson ” – (a pseudonym) alleges in a lawsuit that Trump raped and sexually abused her on multiple occassions in 1994, when she was just 13-years-old. At an Epstein party in New York, she states that she was ordered to strip down to her underwear, massage Epstein, and touch Trump’s penis. Trump and Epstein argued over who would take her virginity, with Epstein getting angry and “violently raping her” when he found out Trump had already done so.

Johnson also alleges that Trump and Epstein threatened to kill her if she went to the authorities, stating “we will make you disappear like [name redacted].”

In a separate complaint , Johnson said that, on another occasion, she pleaded with Trump to wear a condom, to which he struck her in the face and screamed that he “would do whatever he wanted.” After he finished, Johnson claimed that Trump threw money at her and screamed “get a fucking abortion.”

Jane Doe 4 – Another 13-year-old allegedly assaulted by Trump was Jane Doe 4. She told the FBI that, in 1983, she bit Trump while performing oral sex on him, in response to which he hit her in the face. She said that Epstein flew her to New York City on multiple occasions, where she was offered up as “fresh meat” at “intimate gatherings with other, prominent, wealthy men,” where she was “brutally and forcibly battered, assaulted, and raped by these other men.”

Stacey Williams – Williams, a Sports Illustrated swimsuit model, dated Epstein in the 1990s. While at Trump’s Christmas party at the Plaza Hotel, she said that Trump groped her in front of Epstein. “His hands were all over me. They were on my breasts, they were on my butt, they were on, you know, my hips, up and down,” she said. Epstein berated her for letting Trump touch her.

Jill Harth – Harth alleges that in 1993, Trump bundled her into his daughter’s bedroom at Mar-a-Lago, kissed and groped her, and prevented her from leaving.

Jane Doe 1 – At just 14-years-old, Epstein brought her to Trump’s Mar-a-Lago property, telling him “this is a good one, huh?” to which Trump responded “Yes.” She described in detail the sexual abuse she received from Epstein and others, but did not name Trump as one of those individuals.

Maria Farmer – Epstein’s former assistant alleges that, while at the financier’s New York City office, Donald Trump marched into the office in an imposing “predatory” manner. Epstein then appeared and told Trump that Farmer was “not for you,” escorting him to another room where Farmer believes another girl was waiting. She also stated that Trump said he “thought she was 16” although she was actually 25 at the time.

“ Kate ” – Kate (another pseudonym) states that Epstein’s partner Ghislaine Maxwell introduced her to Trump, “with the clear understanding that she was available for sex.” This sex, she said, did not happen. However, in 1997, the British tabloid, The Sunday Mirror, ran a story reporting how “America’s best known billionaire Donald Trump has fallen under the spell of a 20-year-old English girl” (Kate). It also noted that Maxwell had “introduced several of her attractive friends” to Trump. The Sunday Mirror was owned by Ghislaine’s father, Robert Maxwell , until his death in 1991.

Many of these allegations were already publicly available. But the fact that they are appearing in an official government publication is highly significant, especially as the report concludes that “there is more than enough evidence” against Trump and that he “must be investigated and prosecuted.”

It also goes into detail analyzing what it sees as a “relentless” Trump Department of Justice cover-up in order to protect the president. In vociferously defending themselves, the report notes, Trump and his team have been caught telling “brazen lies” about his relationship with Epstein.

Among those, it notes, is Trump’s claim that he kicked Epstein out of Mar-a-Lago after he was caught being a “creep”. This assertion, it notes, is contradicted by Trump himself. A 2009 document detailing a conversation between Trump, his Mar-a-Lago manager and his legal team shows that Trump admitted and his manager confirmed that Epstein “was never asked to leave” the premises. “This document remains under redaction in the DOJ database, in clear violation of federal law,” the House report notes.

In 2024, Trump also took to social media to insist that he was “never on Epstein’s plane.” Yet flight records show that he, in fact, flew at least eight different times on the “Lolita Express” during the 1990s alone.

Furthermore, the report takes aim at Trump’s Department of Justice, which, it claims, has attempted to obfuscate the truth and prevent the public from knowing more about the case. “To cover up” Trump’s relationship to Epstein, it states, the “DOJ has actively obstructed the Epstein investigation into any co-conspirators, attempted to prevent the release of the Epstein files, and then released an incomplete and heavily redacted set to the public—all while withholding key information about Trump in the process.”

As a result, it concludes, the DOJ has effectively “given a pass to all the individuals who took part in this decades-long, multibillion-dollar international sex trafficking ring that victimized over 1,000 women and girls.”

While the report makes many explosive allegations and explicitly calls for a special investigation and prosecution, it is unlikely that it will lead to real consequences, at least in the short term. The report was authored by House Democrats, who are the minority in Congress, and are unable to compel witness testimony or solicit documents through subpoenas without some Republican support. Few Republicans have voiced support for more transparency into Epstein, and those who have, such as Thomas Massie or Marjorie Taylor Greene, have been attacked and marginalized by the party.

The potential for the investigation could dramatically change if Democrats win back power in either chamber, but it would rely on them following through on their rhetoric and actually prosecuting the president. Historically, Democrats have shown little interest in declaring a political civil war. This is compounded by former president Bill Clinton’s own ties to Epstein.

The White House brushed off the report as “nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements.”

It remains completely uncertain whether Trump will face real consequences as a result of this report. What is clear, however, is that his relationship with the world’s most notorious pedophile sex trafficker is a lot closer than many people understand.

MintPress News has been closely covering the development of the Epstein story. Our “ Too Big to Fail ” series details Epstein’s connections with U.S. intelligence and foreign intelligence, and organized crime, and how sexualized blackmail became an institutionalized tool of the national security state.

Earlier this year, we published an investigation detailing the close relationship between Epstein and star academic Noam Chomsky, the latter considering Epstein to be his “best friend.”

For more on the Maxwell family’s close connections to U.S. and Israeli state power, read our investigation , “The CIA, Mossad, and Epstein: Unraveling the Intelligence Ties of The Maxwell Family.”

And to catch up on recent Epstein-related news, read our recent report , “Ten Epstein Revelations You Might Have Missed.”

He is now head of YouTube Music, and is working with the U.S. State Department on a new program directly modeled on the CIA’s successful Cold War-era attempts to use American artists to help force through color revolutions in targeted countries., hip-hop, rap, Universal Music Group, YouTube Lyor Cohen, YouTube Music,
scraped.author: Alan Macleod
scraped.h1: Lyor Cohen: The Shady Israeli Executive Running YouTube Music & the Global Hip Hop Industry
scraped.body_text:
When most people are asked “who controls hip hop?” they are unlikely to think of a 67-year-old Israeli Zionist who comes from a family of Israeli spies and state officials. But Lyor Cohen is the real deal. The brash, cigar-smoking 6 ft 5 in head of YouTube Music is the undisputed king of rap, and arguably the most important and influential person in the entire music business.

Entering his fifth decade in the industry, Cohen began his career as the manager of legendary rap group, Run-DMC, and has launched the career of countless hip hop acts, including LL Cool J, Public Enemy, De La Soul, Slick Rick, A Tribe Called Quest, the Beastie Boys, and DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince (Will Smith).

He later moved beyond just rap and worked with stars like Bon Jovi, Mariah Carey, Nickelback, The Killers, Shania Twain, and Elvis Costello.

Throughout his career, Cohen has pushed hip hop to become more profitable and corporate-friendly, and has worked hard to root out what he sees as anti-semitism in the industry, and ensure that the medium does not become a vehicle for revolutionary change or Palestine solidarity.

MintPress explores the story of how a white Israeli-American came to dominate rap.

This is part of a series of investigations examining the relationship between the U.S. national security state and hip hop music. “ From Fight the Power to Work for It: Chuck D, Public Enemy and How the CIA Neutralized Rap ” explained how Washington works with American musicians to promote regime change in foreign countries.

“ Rappers For Regime Change: How the CIA Recruits Hip Hop Artists Around the World ” exposed a large network of political rappers quietly on the CIA payroll, promoted by the agency to lead color revolutions across the planet.

“Pull up to the curb, drop head, 2-door Rollsing

Dior posing, couldn’t be more chosen

If not, make sure you Warn a Brother, Lyor Cohen”

– Vado, feat. Ludacris and Jadakiss, “Check Em Out”

“Rap mogul” was in many ways an unlikely career path for Lyor Cohen. Born in New York in 1959 to Elisha Cohen, an Israeli secret agent, and Ziva Sirkis, an official at the Israeli Embassies to the United States and United Nations, Lyor spent his formative years living in the Israeli settlement of Kfar Haim, near Netanya. Kfar Haim was named after Haim Arlosoroff, a Zionist negotiator who worked with Nazi Germany in the 1930s, transferring German Jews and their assets to historic Palestine.

Although he attended the University of Miami and lived in the U.S. for the majority of his life, he has never shaken his Israeli accent. Cohen grew up privileged, living in the former Hollywood home of comedian Chico Marx. These features made him stand out even more in the world of 1980s rap music.

After graduating, his mother secured him a job at Israeli state-owned financial institution, Bank Leumi. In the wake of the 1978-1979 Revolution, his primary responsibility was assisting Iranian Jews get their money out of the country and into Israeli hands.

Yet Cohen had his heart set on a much more interesting career. His big break in the music industry came after he met brothers Joseph and Russell Simmons. Joseph was one-third of up-and-coming hip hop crew, Run-DMC. Russell co-founded fledgling record label Def Jam and ran Rush, an arts management company responsible for looking after a number of big-name acts.

In 1984, Cohen joined Rush, working as a road manager for Run-DMC, and helping to manage and promote the Beastie Boys, LL Cool J, Public Enemy, and other acts. He quickly worked his way up the ranks, becoming president, CEO, and a major shareholder in Def Jam Records. There, he helped launch the careers of a host of household names, including Ludacris, Redman, Eric B. and Rakim, and DMX. He also began working with Jay-Z after Def Jam bought out Roc-A-Fella records in 1997.

It is no exaggeration to state that Cohen was primarily responsible for mainstreaming rap and turning Def Jam Records into a powerhouse and a cultural touchstone.

By 1999, he and Russell Simmons decided to sell their remaining shares in the company, pocketing a reported $130 million between them. The buyer was a conglomerate that would ultimately become Universal Music Group. Cohen joined Universal and became the head of Island Records, a legendary label that sported the likes of Bon Jovi, Mariah Carey, and Sir Elton John on its roster.

In 2004, he moved to Warner Music, becoming its CEO and president, and mentored the next generation of music executives, such as Julie Greenwald and Todd Moscowitz.

By 2012, however, the music industry was rapidly changing, and Cohen was ready for a new challenge, founding independent entity, 300 Entertainment. The number “300” was a reference to the 300 Spartan warriors who fought at the Battle of Thermopylae, and symbolized Cohen’s vision that a small team of committed and capable individuals could take on the calcifying, backward major labels and win. 300 launched the careers of a number of notable rappers, including Young Thug and Megan Thee Stallion. Warner Music eventually bought the company out for $400 million in 2021.

Cohen was long gone by then, however, as in 2016, he took on his most influential role yet: that of global head of music for Google and Youtube. Over one billion people listen to music on YouTube alone, including 125 million premium paid listeners. In this position, Cohen holds considerable influence over what the world listens to, which artists are promoted, and who is demoted.

In addition, he currently serves on the board of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and of the National Independent Venues Association, a group of some 1,500 entertainment venues across America.

Throughout his more than four decades in the business, Cohen has developed a reputation as a hard-nosed negotiator with a talent for spotting stars and making money. In 1986, when rap was aggressively not profit orientated, he brokered a historic $1 million marketing deal between Run-DMC and Adidas, the sports apparel company seeing significant increases in shoe sales after the rap group released their hit track “My Adidas.” The moment was described in Rolling Stone magazine as hip hop’s “tipping point,” where the medium crossed over from the underground into the corporate mainstream.

Cohen also pioneered a financial agreement less popular in the industry: the 360 contract. Before the 360 deal, record labels paid for the recording, manufacturing and distribution of music. In return, they took a cut (usually a majority) of the profits from said sales. Artists would make their money primarily through touring and merchandise sales. The 360 deal, in contrast, took a cut of every conceivable revenue stream an artist had, including ticket sales, merchandise, image rights, movie appearances, and advertising deals. Many complained that 360 deals left seemingly popular and successful artists broke or even in debt.

“Like Lyor Cohen, thoughts start flowin’ when I hear a Def Jam”

– MC Jin, 100 Thousand Sold Pt. 2

Cohen has used his considerable influence to shape rap and to promote causes close to him, including that of Israel and anti-Semitism. During the 2024 election campaign, he donated to the Democratic Majority for Israel (DMFI), a lobbying group that funds right-wing pro-Israel Democrats and attacks candidates advocating for Palestinian rights or statehood.

In 2021, for example, the DMFI endorsed little-known but staunchly pro-Israel candidate Shontel Brown in her contentious face-off for Ohio’s 11th congressional district against Nina Turner, a democratic socialist, national co-chair of Bernie Sanders’ 2020 election campaign, and an outspoken critic of Israel’s policies.

Vast amounts of pro-Israel money flowed into Brown’s campaign, helping her to defeat Turner. In her acceptance speech, Brown praised Israel and later thanked the Jewish community for “help[ing] me get over the finish line.”

The DMFI ran the same playbook against Jamaal Bowman and Cori Bush, and the organization continues to play a key role in stamping out left-wing insurgents within the Democratic Party.

Cohen has also opened his checkbook to directly bankroll pro-Israel Democrats, including Hillary Clinton, Barack Obama, Chuck Schumer and Cory Booker.

In October of 2023, Cohen – who usually avoids the limelight – took to the stage at the Spirit of Life gala in Los Angeles to denounce Hamas’ “brutality” “slaughtering innocent children, women, and men, just because they were Jewish,” and call for a release of captured Israelis.

He later signed an open letter decrying opposition to Israel’s actions in Gaza as inherently racist anti-semitism.

“Hamas, Iran, and their allies and ideological sympathizers in the West have flooded the world with their hateful lies and antisemitic incitement since October 7 — lies designed to demonize Israel, the Jewish people, and their supporters,” the letter begins, taking aim at, “well-meaning celebrities and public figures have been manipulated by this constant stream of misinformation, which they have also helped to amplify.”

The statement’s claims become increasingly extremist themselves, claiming that the phrase “Free Palestine” is “a call to violence” against Jews. Cohen and the other signatories categorically reject that Israel is carrying out a genocide, arguing that accusing Israel of such crimes is a disgusting “blood libel.”

At the same time, however, they insist that the October 7 attacks themselves constitute a “genocidal war on Israel,” and that Hamas alone is responsible for all the deaths caused. “The suffering of civilians in Gaza is a strategy of Hamas,” they explain, as Hamas “leav[es] women and children above ground to be used as their human shields.”

Perhaps the most extreme and contentious statement that Cohen signed onto frames Israel’s murder of hundreds of journalists as justified. “The vast majority of ‘journalists’ pumping out propaganda in Gaza are, in fact, members or supporters of the terrorist organizations themselves,” it claims.

The letter was organized by the Creative Community for Peace (CCP) and signed by many of the most influential executives in the music industry, including multibillionaire entertainment kingpin Haim Saban, Spirit Music Group chairman, David Renzer, and former Atlantic Records Group CEO, Julie Greenwald.

The CCP – an organization MintPress has previously profiled – is an entertainment industry pressure group working to oppose the Boycott Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, and stymie anti-Israel sentiment within the field more generally.

“It’s summertime, but it’s like snowin’ in my watch.

Check the Funk Doc, the Lyor Cohen of the block.”

–DJ Envy feat. Redman, “So Vicious”.

Cohen’s parents were, if anything, even more involved with the defense and promotion of Israel than their son. Ziva Serkis met Elisha Cohen when she was a nurse tending to his headwounds sustained during the Nakhba – the 1948 ethnic cleansing of around 750,000 Palestinians that allowed for the creation of the State of Israel.

Elisha was a member of the elite Palmach strike force and served in the Harel Brigade, commanded by future prime minister Yitzhak Rabin. The Harel Brigade is infamous for its many crimes in 1948, including carrying out biological warfare against the region’s indigenous population.

After the war, the Cohens moved to New York City, where both would work at the Israeli Embassy, Ziva as an official, and Elisha as security. They would later divorce.

After the 1968 war, Israeli fighters, security, and secret agents were in high demand across the world, and Elisha moved to Nigeria to work on a number of projects. There, he let it be known that he was working for Israeli state intelligence outlets, Shin Bet and the Mossad.

Cohen, an investigation from Israeli outlet Haaretz claimed , spent much of his time building close relations with senior officers in the Nigerian military. But he also forged ties with anti-government rebels in the secessionist state of Biafra.

As the brutal civil war was raging in Nigeria, he was captured by General Olusegun Obasanjo, who accused him of building installations and providing smuggling equipment to the rebels. Far from denying it, Cohen responded “we can also build for you” – a response that evidently impressed Obasanjo.

Cohen spent many years working with the Nigerian military and, in 1984, just as his son, Lyor, was leaving his job at the Israeli bank to try to make it in the music industry, Elisha returned to Nigeria for perhaps his most controversial job yet.

A military coup the previous year had catapulted many of Elisha’s old contacts into senior positions in the government. They wanted him to find and kidnap the previous Minister for Transportation, Dr. Umaru Dikko, who had become a scapegoat for the new regime. For this, Cohen was to be paid between $3-5 million.

Dikko had fled to London, so Cohen put together a crack team of Israeli and Nigerian operatives to carry out the intercontinental operation. On July 4, 1984, as he was leaving his home, Cohen’s team surrounded Dikko, bundled him into a van, and drugged him with sedatives. The plan was to keep him sedated, force him into a diplomatic crate and place him into a Nigerian cargo plane waiting at London’s Stansted Airport. He would then be flown to Nigeria, where Cohen and the military junta were waiting.

The plan failed, however, because Dikko’s secretary unexpectedly arrived at his address, just as the incident was occurring, and notified local police, who ignored the diplomatic cargo identifications, and released him.

The event caused a worldwide scandal. The four operatives on the ground (three Israeli and one Nigerian) were quickly arrested, and given long prison sentences. But as soon as British authorities identified Cohen as the mastermind, the U.K. Ministry of Defence unexpectedly shut the investigation down entirely.

Although there has never been any official confirmation that Cohen was indeed a Mossad or Shin Bet operative, his second wife, Susan, continued to believe that he was.

“CEO? The next Lyor, no, the next leader of the whole free world!”

– Jay Z., “Ignorant Shit”

Lyor Cohen has a long history of using his influence to wheedle out artists with problematic viewpoints. In 1989, he successfully pressured Public Enemy frontman Chuck D to fire band member Professor Griff after he made controversial and anti-semitic remarks to The Washington Times.

Griff, the band’s “Minister for Information,” was responsible for most of Public Enemy’s political direction, infusing it with the message of Malcolm X, the Nation of Islam, and the Black Panthers. With Griff gone, Public Enemy’s message became significantly less radical, to the point where today, Chuck D and Lyor Cohen have teamed up with the State Department to use rap music to promote regime change around the world.

Shortly after Griff’s defenestration, another band member, Flavor Flav, went through a number of controversial incidents. In 1991, he pled guilty and was imprisoned for domestic violence. Two years later, he was charged with attempted murder and imprisoned for shooting his neighbor. He also was at the center of a string of other domestic violence cases (including one where he tried to stab a child) there were no calls for him to be censured, and he remains in Public Enemy to this day.

Lupe Fiasco’s career was similarly derailed by Cohen, at least in his own telling. The rapper said that Cohen attempted to pressure him into signing an onerous 360 deal, suggesting his future would be in jeopardy if he did not agree. “Lyor was like, ‘Yo if you don’t sign this 360 deal, we’re not promoting your records,’” he said . “I didn’t sign, and my career was like ‘goodbye’. My career ended at [my third album] ‘Lasers,’” he said.

Lupe Fiasco is a passionate supporter of Palestinian liberation, regularly sporting the flag at his shows. One of his most critically acclaimed songs, “Words I Never Said,” included a searing critique of U.S. foreign policy: “Limbaugh is a racist, Glenn Beck is a racist. Gaza Strip was getting bombed, Obama didn’t say shit.”

Despite being critically acclaimed as one of the most skilled lyricists in the business, Lupe Fiasco’s career did indeed begin to nosedive after “Lasers” and “Words I Never Said.” He became increasingly jaded with the industry, and, in 2016, directly referenced Cohen’s treatment of him in the freestyle track, “N.E.R.D.” where he said, “Artists gettin’ robbed for their publishing by dirty Jewish execs who think that it’s alms from the covenant.”

The backlash to the freestyle was intense. After the Anti-Defamation League publicly condemned him, the track was pulled from Soundcloud for hate speech. His upcoming albums were cancelled, and he announced his retirement from making new music (although he would later return).

A similar occurrence happened to Yasiin Bey (a.k.a. Mos Def). Bey, who, like Fiasco, is Muslim, also addressed the power and influence of those at the top of the music industry in his song, “The Rape Over,” obliquely referencing Cohen in the lyrics:

“Old white men is runnin’ this rap shit

Corporate forces runnin’ this rap shit

Some tall Israeli is runnin’ this rap shit

We poke out our asses for a chance to cash in”

Like with Fiasco, the song was immediately denounced as hate speech, including by the Creative Community for Peace, and was essentially banned, being removed from his album by the record company.

“Tell Lyor I need a million for my monologues. A small price for my cocaine catalog.”

–Pusha T. “Cook it Down (Freestyle)”

Cohen is undoubtedly brilliant and successful at what he does. His tactics and negotiating styles are legendary, but have made him many enemies over the years. Social media is festooned with videos of rappers recounting their run-ins with him.

Beanie Sigel, for instance, stated Cohen’s brash insults and his insinuation that he was illiterate caused him to pull a gun on him. Big Daddy Kane said he and his crew almost lynched Cohen. And Suge Knight spat in his face after Cohen lowballed him during a business negotiation.

Method Man complained that Cohen’s predatory tactics have left rappers broke, while he sits on a net worth rumored to be north of $170 million . “How many old artists and entertainers are left with the bag? It’s not many of them. But you have still got your Lyor Cohen’s who have still got the bag,” he said . “How the fuck did we get back to minus – not even a whole fucking penny but a portion of a penny – and the rest going to someone who doesn’t even make music at all? He just has a platform?” he added.

Roc-A-Fella Records co-founder Damon Dash, a longtime associate of Cohen, has gone further, describing him as a “culture vulture” – someone from outside a culture who is there to exploit it for profit. Dash accuses Cohen of looking past Black candidates to appoint Jews like Julie Greenwald and Todd Moscowitz to top positions in hip hop, despite their lack of knowledge or familiarity with the genre in order “to further control our culture.” “He is the cancer for the culture,” he told The Joe Budden Podcast.

Cohen admits that he can be a tough negotiator, but rejects any accusation of serious impropriety. “I’m a carnivore — I’m not a vegan. I’m a predator. But I don’t do anything illegal,” he told The Financial Times.

“Your mind I’m blowin’, cash I’m stowin’, without you knowin’

While I rustle up dough like Lyor Cohen”

– Nice & Smooth, “Hot Shit”

Cohen’s position at Google and YouTube is surely the most influential post he has held. As the company’s global head of music, he helps shape tastes and curate what the public around the world listens to. And he has used this position to willingly team up with the United States Department of State to use music as a vehicle to push for regime change across the planet.

In 2024, Cohen and Secretary of State Antony Blinken jointly announced the creation of the new Global Music Partnership program, a scheme directly modeled on the CIA’s successful Cold War-era attempts to use American artists to help force through color revolutions in targeted countries.

In the Congo, the CIA used a U.S. government-sponsored Louis Armstrong tour as a cover to send its agents deep into the country, gathering information on newly-elected president, Patrice Lumumba. The CIA considered Lumumba an “African Fidel Castro” and worked to successfully assassinate him, plunging the country into decades of dictatorship, from which it has never recovered.

Meanwhile, the CIA flooded Eastern Europe with American music with more than a hint of regime change about it.

Referencing these events, Blinken said during the program’s announcement, that “America’s secret weapon is a blue note and a minor chord. Music is such a powerful diplomatic force because, I think, it taps into something fundamental, universal.” “In Berlin, just before the wall came down, Bruce Springsteen played to the adoration of countless fans.”

Cohen said he was pleased to be helping the State Department “leverage global events.” “We will utilize major international gatherings to inspire action,” he added. What exact sort of “global events” and “actions” Blinken and Cohen had in mind are open to interpretation.

A number of rappers, including Chuck D and Armani White signed on to the program, despite its history of being used to depose Black leaders.

“The Lyor Cohen of Dior Homme

That’s ‘Dior Homme,’ not ‘Dior, homie’

The crib Scarface, could it be more Tony?

You love me for me, could you be more phony?”

–Kanye West feat. Rick Ross, “Devil in a New Dress.”

Today, Cohen is just one of a host of Israelis in senior, influential positions at YouTube. The company’s longtime vice-president and chief marketing officer for Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Latin America, Riki Drori , is a former Israeli soldier, consulate communications manager, and chief communications advisor for Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin. Meanwhile, YouTube’s global head of crater programs, Netta Gross , is a former Israeli military space satellite officer.

More worrying is the trend of YouTube promoting ex-Israeli spies to the upper echelons of its organization. One example of this is product strategy and operations executive Naama Citron-Topf , whose LinkedIn profile notes she received the Unit 8200 Award of Excellence while serving in Israel. Unit 8200 is the Israeli Defense Forces’ most elite spying organization, responsible for cyberwarfare and psychological operations worldwide.

“Dior Cold when I got ice on,

Lyor Cohen, plus I got the hype y’all feed off”

–Lady London and Mila J, “D4M”

Music has always been a battleground. And many industry executives have made Israel a centerpiece of their politics, attempting to promote the Jewish State and attack its opponents at every opportunity.

Billionaire entertainment executive Haim Saban, for example, is the largest individual fundraiser for the Friends of the Israeli Defense Forces (FIDF), a charity that raises money to buy equipment for IDF soldiers. “I’m a one-issue guy, and my issue is Israel,” he said . He has supported AIPAC and attacked Democrats insufficiently enthusiastic about the country. In 2010, he attempted to pressure CBS to ditch Oliver Stone’s documentary series and pushed the industry to cancel him due to what Saban considered Stone’s anti-Semitic beliefs. He is widely identified as being the author of President Joe Biden’s Israel policy.

Another executive working to promote Israel’s image is Cohen’s longtime partner at Rush and Def Jam, Russell Simmons. Emails published by Wikileaks show that Simmons was part of a large clique of entertainment executives working alongside Israeli government and military officials behind the scenes to promote Israel. Some even worked on a conspiracy to cancel left-wing film director Ken Loach.

Simmons specifically worked on improving Israel’s floundering image among the Black community. When asked if he had any ideas on how to do this, he said , “Simple messaging from non Jews specifically from Muslims promoting peace and Israel’s right to exist…We have resources and the desire to win rather than lose the hearts of young Muslims and Jews.”

What these resources were, he explained:

“We have hundreds of collaboration programs between Imams Rabbis and their congregations. We have many respected imams who would join former chief rabbi metzker [sic] rabbi Schneier and non Jews in promoting the Saudi peace plan.”

“Through this campaign we will be helping Israel,” he concluded.

In short, then, hip hop is a product of African American culture. But it is not owned and controlled by that community. Lyor Cohen helped shape the genre more than perhaps any other individual. The son of an Israeli secret agent and a state official has put his own stamp on the music, and worked hard to eradicate anti-semitism in the industry. He has also made his views on Israel and Palestine well known. More concerning still is his collaboration with the State Department on regime change and psychological operations masquerading as cultural programs. Yasiin Bey is right: this tall Israeli really does run the rap game.

scraped.body_text:
Texas Democrats are not wasting time following far-left Democrat Gina Hinojosa’s stunning win in the gubernatorial race on Tuesday, where she unseated longtime GOP governor Greg Abbott.

On Friday, Houston Mayor John Whitmire announced during a press conference that he is altering his city’s policy toward ICE by changing how Houston police officers handle immigration-related checks.

“We will change our policy regarding contact with ICE,” Whitmire said . “I do this to begin a healing process and reduce fear and anxiety across our community.”

“I also do this knowing that elections matter,” he added.

WATCH:

After Democrats swept statewide elections in Texas, Houston Mayor John Whitmire said Friday he has directed the Houston Police Department to change its policy on contact with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement , saying the move is intended to reduce fear and anxiety in the community.🔗https://t.co/VGa4Oo0CnE

— Houston Chronicle (@HoustonChron) November 6, 2026

Here’s more from KHOU regarding how the new policy will limit ICE activities:

According to Whitmire, the changes are intended to prevent routine encounters with Houston police from leading to immigration-related warrant checks unless a person is being charged with a new jail offense.

Diaz explained that the new policy means officers will no longer contact ICE solely because someone has an administrative immigration warrant if that person is not being arrested.

For example, if an officer pulls someone over for a minor traffic violation and issues a citation, that person can go about their day without HPD contacting ICE, even if an administrative ICE warrant exists.

However, officers will still contact ICE if someone is arrested for a jail offense and also has an administrative ICE warrant.

This is just the first step in Texas Democrats’ efforts to throw the door back open for illegal immigrants to flood into the Lone Star State.

As Fox News notes , Hinojosa has called on Abbott to end state and local cooperation with ICE, and she can order that on day one.

Hinojosa also voted against SB 4 in 2017 as a TX state rep. The bill was essentially a sanctuary cities ban and required TX law enforcement to cooperate with ICE detainers. She then voted against another SB 4 in 2023, which made it a state crime to cross Texas illegally.

It’s going to be a long four years for the 30 million-plus residents in this former GOP stronghold.

scraped.body_text:
The woke left is in an uproar after a professional athlete expressed his displeasure over the red-green takeover of America earlier this week.

As The New York Post reported , Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander was not happy that disgraced Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed prevailed on Tuesday night.

scraped.h1: Antifa bike ride targets Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia — on eve of Kristallnacht anniversary
scraped.body_text:
A statement from the organizer specifically says 'Zionist' businesses should leave the city.

Local leaders in Pennsylvania are condemning a demonstration targeting Jewish businesses on the eve of the 88th anniversary of the infamous Kristallnacht attacks in Nazi Germany.

The self-described "Anti-fascist" group Philly Bike on Your Left has promoted the ride, and a flyer that the group posted on social media specifically cites Jewish-owned businesses and crosses them out.

'As the political ideology of Zionism dies a long deserved death these businesses will die with it. Free Palestine.'

"NO BUSINESS FOR ZIONISTS!" read the text on the flyer. "THESE ZIONIST ESTABLISHMENTS MUST GO! NOT IN OUR CITY!"

The ride is scheduled for Sunday at noon.

The flyer did not mention Kristallnacht, but the boycott will be held just one day from the 88th anniversary of the violent attacks on Jewish people and businesses.

The groups behind the boycott said in a statement online they want to show solidarity with the Palestinian cause. They also called the action an "anti-fascist" operation and insisted that "conflating Zionism with Judaism" is "disingenuous."

"As the political ideology of Zionism dies a long deserved death these businesses will die with it. Free Palestine," the statement concluded.

Philadelphia Democrat Mayor Cherelle Parker was among those who condemned the ride.

"As Mayor, I serve every Philadelphian under the explicit premise that freedom of speech and freedom from fear are not competing values," she wrote in a lengthy statement. "No one should be targeted, threatened, or made to feel unwelcome because of their faith, identity, or background. Every person deserves to feel safe and respected in the city they call home."

She went on to say singling out businesses because the owners are Jewish is "unacceptable" and has no place in Philadelphia.

"Let me be clear: safety is non-negotiable," she continued.

"Anyone who engages in threats, intimidation, or unlawful conduct will beheld accountable. One Philly, A United City will always mean that every Philadelphian can feel safe, respected, and welcome, with no place for threats, intimidation, or harassment."

RELATED: Videos capture Palestinian activists screaming at Mamdani: 'Opportunist piece of s**t!'

Parker said local law enforcement would coordinate to maintain safety and order during the demonstration.

Democrat Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania called on "every Democrat of conscience" to "condemn this sick parade of rank antisemitism."

Commissioner Jeffrey Nash characterized the boycott as an "appalling act of hatred, bigotry, and intimidation towards the Jewish community."

Some of the businesses targeted will remain open to defy the intimidation from the groups.

scraped.description: More than 50 years after Title IX, girls are fighting to keep biological males out of their sports.
scraped.author: https://www.facebook.com/140738092630206
scraped.h1: NO LEAGUE OF THEIR OWN? Trans athletes force women to fight for what they've already won.
scraped.body_text:
More than 50 years after Title IX, girls are fighting to keep biological males out of their sports.

Do you ever notice ... how something women spent decades fighting for now requires an election to keep?

A league of their own.

A national organization cannot be the only voice your daughter hears defending her. Moms and dads need to stand up in their own communities.

Not a guaranteed championship. Not a participation trophy.

A fair chance to compete against other females. Apparently, we need to count the ballots on that.

Girls shouldn’t need an election to have their own sports. But here we are.

On November 3, voters in Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska, and Washington considered measures addressing sex-based athletic eligibility.

Different proposals, different provisions, but a common question: Will we preserve female sports categories for females?

Voters in Nebraska, Arizona, and Washington approved ballot measures prohibiting boys from participating in girls’ sports. Proposition 134, a similar measure in Colorado, was also leading as votes continued to be counted.

My wife and I attended an election-night watch party with supporters of Protect Kids Colorado , the grassroots organization behind Proposition 134 and two other ballot measures.

Chaired by XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey, Protect Kids Colorado helped organize the effort behind Proposition 134 alongside local moms Erin Lee, Lori Gimelshteyn, and other concerned parents.

The room was filled with volunteers and supporters, hopeful and energized as the results trickled in.

These folks had worked hard.

More than 3,300 petition circulators helped qualify the organization's three measures for the ballot, with 170,000 Coloradans signing its petitions.

They knocked on doors, visited churches, and talked with their neighbors.

And catch this: October campaign finance reports showed roughly $4.4 million raised by opponents, compared with about $216,000 supporting the effort.

About 20 to 1.

Apparently, concerned parents didn’t get the memo that they were supposed to be overwhelmed.

And guess what?

As of Wednesday morning, Proposition 134 was leading with roughly 52% of the vote, although the outcome remained uncalled.

But this story started long before anyone ordered campaign signs.

Women fought for years to get their daughters onto playing fields, into gymnasiums, and onto college rosters.

They fought for equipment, practice time, coaching, and scholarships.

Representatives Patsy Mink and Edith Green and Senator Birch Bayh helped carry that fight into Congress .

President Richard Nixon signed Title IX on June 23, 1972.

Its prohibition against sex discrimination extended across federally funded education, with athletics becoming one of its most consequential applications.

Implementation required years of additional pressure and litigation.

Before Title IX, girls accounted for roughly 294,000 high school sports participation entries. In 2025-2026, that figure exceeded 3.65 million .

Pause on that for a moment.

That is an extraordinary achievement.

Yet, now we’re arguing over whether the category that helped make that progress possible should remain female.

We finally opened the gym doors for girls.

Then some adults apparently forgot why there were separate teams inside.

Biological sex matters in sports.

Boys are male. Girls are female. Period.

Identifying differently does not change that.

Hormones and surgery can alter physical characteristics. But they do not change a male into a biological female.

The American College of Sports Medicine identifies biological sex as a major determinant of athletic performance.

Its consensus statement explains how male puberty produces substantial differences in muscle mass, strength, power, oxygen-carrying capacity, and other physical characteristics relevant to competition.

Before puberty, performance differences are much smaller. That doesn’t mean every boy beats every girl.

It explains why we have girls’ teams.

We understand competitive categories when weight classes are involved.

Nobody tells a lightweight boxer that objecting to a heavyweight opponent demonstrates a disappointing lack of inclusion.

Yet girls are expected to accept a comparable dismissal of the physical differences their category exists to recognize.

These are actual girls with actual consequences.

We know Riley Gaines , who became a national advocate after tying Lia Thomas at the NCAA championships.

We remember Italian Olympic boxer Angela Carini abandoning her Paris bout after just 46 seconds, overwhelmed by powerful punches from Imane Khelif.

The fight intensified the controversy over why the IOC permitted him to compete after a previous disqualification over sex eligibility.

We saw fencer Stephanie Turner take a knee rather than compete against an opponent identifying as female, receiving a disqualification for refusing the bout.

In Connecticut, runners Selina Soule, Chelsea Mitchell, Alanna Smith, and Ashley Nicoletti challenged a policy allowing male athletes who identify as female to compete in girls’ track.

Their attorneys report that two such competitors collected 15 girls’ state titles between 2017 and 2020.

Their lawsuit concerns lost honors and competitive opportunities, not an abstract disagreement over terminology.

Then there is Payton McNabb , the North Carolina volleyball player struck in the face by a ball spiked by a transgender opponent in 2022.

McNabb has described sustaining a concussion and lasting problems, including impaired vision and partial paralysis.

Sports involve injuries. Everybody knows that.

The question is why adults should require girls to accept additional concerns about physical mismatches while treating their objections as the real problem.

And girls should not have to sustain a serious injury before somebody decides their concerns deserve a hearing.

The issue follows them into the privacy of a locker room.

Former University of Pennsylvania swimmer Paula Scanlan testified that administrators told the women that Lia Thomas’ participation and presence in their locker room were nonnegotiable.

When the women objected, they were offered psychological services to become comfortable undressing in front of a male.

Scanlan summed up the university’s response this way: “We, the women, were the problem, not the victims.”

Let that settle in.

The women raised concerns about their own privacy.

The university decided that it was the women who needed adjusting. Apparently, the boundaries that needed moving were theirs.

In 2025, Penn entered a federal Title IX resolution agreement that included policy changes and personalized apologies to affected female swimmers.

An apology matters.

So would having listened to them in the first place.

But many more girls have names we don’t know.

The girl who missed qualifying for state.

The girl who lost a college scholarship.

The girl changing in a bathroom stall.

The girl wondering whether speaking up will cost her teammates, friends, or a place on the roster. More of them are finding their voices.

A championship race happens once.

And for many, that is once in a lifetime after years of dedicated training. You cannot give a teenager those starting blocks back at age 30.

They shouldn’t need a national following before the adults in their own community listen.

Here in Colorado, the dispute is still unfolding.

Parents at Dakota Ridge High School have objected after a male student who identifies as female made the girls’ junior varsity volleyball roster while female students were cut.

Their account raises a straightforward question about whose opportunities a girls’ roster is supposed to provide.

Jefferson County Public Schools says its gender-identity policies comply with Colorado law. The federal government says those policies violate Title IX.

In March, the Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights found violations involving female sports, bathrooms, locker rooms, and overnight accommodations.

In June, it issued another warning over the district’s refusal to change course.

President Trump’s February 2025 executive order directed federal agencies to protect female athletic opportunities and locker rooms through Title IX enforcement.

Jefferson County Public Schools continues to resist that enforcement position.

The Supreme Court, meanwhile, upheld Idaho’s and West Virginia’s sex-based sports restrictions in June 2026.

To be precise, it ruled that states may maintain those restrictions; it did not order every state to adopt them.

Which helps explain why Coloradans had Proposition 134 on their ballots.

Jeffco Kids First has helped bring local parents’ concerns into public view. Jeffco’s school board opposed Proposition 134.

Parents shouldn’t need a working knowledge of federal litigation to ask who can try out for their daughter’s volleyball team.

Even the International Olympic Committee has changed course.

Its new female-category policy, beginning with the 2028 Los Angeles Games, limits eligibility to biological females , using a one-time SRY gene screening.

Yet defending female sports can still make you a target at a women’s basketball game.

Ask Jennifer Sey.

Her company, XX-XY Athletics, sells shirts with a simple message: “Refuse to Pretend.”

Sey has been outspoken in support of the Camas cross-country girls who walked away from a race rather than accept their male teammate’s participation in the girls’ category.

That runner has since qualified for the girls’ state championships, finishing seventh at the regional qualifier. That is a place in the girls’ state competition that is now occupied by a male.

When somebody says this affects only a small number of athletes, ask them which girls are supposed to consider their opportunity expendable.

Your daughter?

Or is it OK if it’s somebody else’s child?

RELATED: The WNBA has a tolerance problem — and it’s not coming from the women in XX-XY shirts

Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images

Earlier this WNBA season, security told fans to cover their XX-XY shirts .

At the Finals, Sey recorded the harassment directed at her and her friends, including people telling them to kill themselves.

Security escorted them from their seats for a “conversation,” then allowed them to return.

You would think supporting female sports would be an ordinary position at a women’s basketball game.

Apparently, the shirt needed its own league approval review.

Meanwhile, the WNBA’s collective bargaining agreement says “only players who are women are eligible,” without defining “women” or spelling out transgender eligibility rules.

That leaves the boundary of its female category unresolved.

The league can tell you when a foot crosses the three-point line. You would think it can explain who qualifies for the women’s league.

Moms for Liberty has helped bring these concerns into public view.

Alliance Defending Freedom has represented female athletes, including the Connecticut runners, in their fight for fair competition.

Those efforts make a difference, but a national organization cannot be the only voice your daughter hears defending her. Moms and dads need to stand up in their own communities.

At the school board meeting. In the athletic director’s office.

When policies are written and when their daughters say something is wrong.

A dad can spot a missed holding penalty from the upper deck through somebody’s nachos. Surely he can find his voice when his daughter’s opportunity is on the line.

Show up.

Ask direct questions. Insist on answers.

Support her when she speaks, especially when speaking carries a cost.

We tell our children to stand up for what is right. They ought to see us doing it.

Scott Smith’s daughter was sexually assaulted by a male student in a Loudoun County school bathroom.

The attacker later assaulted another girl after being transferred to a different school. Investigations did not establish that he claimed a female identity to gain entry.

What they did establish was serious institutional failure.

Protecting private spaces also requires acknowledging that access rules can be exploited. Girls should not have to determine whether someone entering their private space is sincere.

And a father demanding accountability should not have to fight an institution more concerned with managing the controversy than answering for what happened.

Nebraska and Arizona have decided.

They are still counting votes in Colorado and Washington. But whatever the final tally, the girls deserve an answer.

Their mothers and grandmothers fought to get them onto the field.

Their daughters should not have to spend their athletic careers in court explaining why that field exists.

Refuse to pretend.

Girls should not have to surrender what women fought so hard to win.

Jonathan Flora

scraped.h1: Will midterm losses clear the way for MAGA’s next generation?
scraped.body_text:
Jonathan Keeperman and Jeremy Carl see a chance to rebuild with a stronger bench after the midterm losses.

After Republicans absorbed a broad midterm defeat that erased their Senate firewall and handed Democrats a large House majority, BlazeTV host Jonathan Keeperman is determined to "make lemonade out of the lemons."

The original MAGA in the 2010s and early 2020s, he says, was hugely successful because it was run by the kind of “outsiders and weirdos and misfits” necessary to “[disrupt] the political stasis.” He suggests that lasting success will require a “suite of experience” and “management skills” the early disruptors largely lacked.

Keeperman hopes the midterms, as brutal as they were, will force a hard discussion about what it will take to make the movement “sustainable” and actually “execute on these promises over the long term.”

“Can we construct an environment where, despite everything that's gone on here, we can bring on really good people, convince them to stay and build something that's durable?” he asks political data analyst Jeremy Carl.

Carl is also positive about the future of MAGA.

“I've been talking a lot with my second oldest son who's looking to maybe try to work in Washington, and what I've sort of told him is actually right now is the best time because all the time servers, all the political hacks, all those guys are going to be running for the hills,” he says.

People often forget, he says, that “the Trump movement is only a decade old in terms of its reshaping of the GOP,” and in that span of time, it’s already “cleared out so much of the dead wood.”

“Now look, in a brush fire like we just had, everything gets cleared out — the dead trees and maybe some healthier green ones,” Carl acknowledges.

Many of those dead trees, he notes, were in favor of the Dignity Act, which would have granted legal status to millions of illegal immigrants.

“I'm not trying to sugarcoat what was really, really bad, but it disproportionately hit some of the bad guys in our party, cleared them out,” says Carl.

“I had a sort of viral tweet on this, where I said, ‘Look if you're a young guy and are interested, politically motivated, there have never in my lifetime ... been as many GOP-leaning congressional seats or state House seats or whatever that are going to be out there for the taking than in this next election cycle coming up,'” he continues.

“That’s the really positive end of the vision.”

To hear more of the conversation, watch the episode above.

To enjoy more of the news through the anthropological lens of Christopher Rufo and Lomez, subscribe to BlazeTV — the largest multi-platform network of voices who love America, defend the Constitution, and live the American dream.

BlazeTV Staff

items.title: Texas rejects the Republican establishment in historic midterm election: What comes next?
items.summary: While Texas has “turned blue," the question remains if we can build a movement powerful enough to demand something fundamentally different.
