scraped.title: The Trump Administration’s Border Wall Strategy: Waive the Laws it Doesn’t Like.
scraped.description: In just a year and a half, the Department of Homeland Security has issued an unprecedented number of waivers of federal laws for border wall construction, threatening the southern border’s fragile ecosystem and the communities that depend on it.
scraped.author: Bala Sivaraman
scraped.h1: The Trump Administration’s Border Wall Strategy: Waive the Laws it Doesn’t Like.
scraped.body_text:
Earthjustice serves hundreds of public-interest clients, providing top-tier legal representation free of charge — and we win. Because the earth needs a good lawyer.

Earthjustice serves hundreds of public-interest clients, providing top-tier legal representation free of charge — and we win. Because the earth needs a good lawyer.

Our Stories

In just a year and a half, the Department of Homeland Security has issued an unprecedented number of waivers of federal laws for border wall construction, threatening the southern border’s fragile ecosystem and the communities that depend on it.

By Bala Sivaraman

The U.S.-Mexico border spans a vast, interconnected region of exceptional ecological, cultural, and economic value. Its deserts, rivers, grasslands, mountains, and coastal habitats support remarkable biodiversity, wildlife migration, and clean water.

Just as important, countless communities on opposite sides of the border are linked by generations of family ties, cultural traditions stretching back millennia, and economic activity critical to the entire U.S. economy. The border is a remarkable place.

But construction of the Trump administration’s border wall is putting that all in jeopardy. The administration intends to use billions of taxpayer dollars to construct its system of land and water barriers across nearly the entire border. That includes many hundreds of miles of double wall or wall paired alongside water barriers.

These plans threaten the communities and biodiversity along the entirety of the U.S.-Mexico border. And in order to advance them, the administration is not just breaking the law, it is waiving the law entirely.

But Earthjustice is fighting back — and winning. In October, a court issued an order immediately halting border wall construction throughout Big Bend National Park in Texas.

Read on to learn more about the Trump administration’s plans and our legal fight to stop them.

A view of the Rio Grande River in Big Bend National Park. (Deb Snelson / Getty Images)

While development of a wall along the southern border was a cornerstone commitment of Trump’s first term, its actual construction was stalled in many places because of a lack of significant funding appropriated by Congress and lawsuits against the administration’s efforts to unlawfully use funds that were set aside for other purposes.

That all changed last year when Congress appropriated $46.5 billion to U.S. Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) for the “construction, installation, or improvement of new or replacement primary, waterborne, and secondary barriers” through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Armed with more than twice the amount of funding than all previous spending on border barrier construction combined, the Trump administration has since doubled down on an obscure authority to speed construction: issuing waivers that allow CBP to blatantly disregard federal and local laws.

Under the 2005 REAL ID Act, the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) is authorized to waive any legal requirements it deems necessary to “ensure expeditious construction of the barriers and roads” along the southern border.

Similar waivers were issued throughout Trump’s first term as well. But the rate at which the second Trump administration has doled out waivers is unprecedented. In the past year and a half, DHS has invoked over 30 waivers , accounting for roughly half the total number the agency has issued in its more than two-decade history.

This push to sideline legal oversight is central to the administration’s goal to build as much wall as quickly as it can.

Bedrock environmental and public health regulations, like the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act, and Endangered Species Act, are the most frequent targets of these exemptions. But other laws have also been waived, including those related to Native American religious freedom, procurement and contracting, and transparency.

By waiving these laws, DHS is giving itself a free pass to ignore the significant, often irreparable consequences of its operations and hide its decisions from the public. Already, wall construction has destroyed habitat for threatened wildlife, desecrated sacred sites, and heightened extreme flooding risks in border towns from Texas to California.

“The reality is that this wall will make our communities less safe and less resilient, and will put people’s lives in danger,” says Martin Castro, watershed science director at the Rio Grande International Study Center (RGISC) in Laredo, Texas.

In October 2025, then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem waived a wide swath of procurement and contracting laws for every single CBP sector, including Laredo. Noem then issued another waiver for the Laredo sector in December that allows CBP to bypass nearly every major environmental law to build border wall in the sector.

Castro warns that the administration’s plan to remove vegetation along the Rio Grande’s banks and install hundreds of miles of buoys and barriers will destroy a unique riparian corridor, home to an abundance of rare native species and drought-tolerant vegetation endemic to the region.

“Removing this vegetation increases soil erosion, sedimentation, and saltation of the river,” Castro stresses, noting that doing so threatens the health of aquatic species and compromises the quality of drinking water for millions of residents along both sides of the border.

But the harms of the wall extend far beyond the environmental impact. The buildout of this network of land and water barriers poses an “inevitable threat to human life, property, and critical bridge infrastructure,” according to a recent report commissioned by RGISC.

The analysis, by geomorphologist Mark Tomkins, PhD, underscores the dangers of erecting such massive infrastructure within a floodplain. It warns that both the wall and buoy system will drastically exacerbate the impacts of floods, causing water levels to rise higher and faster, and sweeping heavy equipment, cars, boats and other hazardous debris downstream. This debris will accumulate under bridges, eroding their support columns and potentially inciting collapse.

Had the government not waived laws like the National Environmental Policy Act and the Clean Water Act for the Laredo sector, it would have had to account for those impacts, consider alternatives that would be less harmful, and respond to public input. Because of the waiver authority, it did not have to conduct any analysis before beginning to implement its plan.

These dangers aren’t hypothetical — they’re already happening . Two bridges along the U.S.-Mexico border had to shut down this summer due to buoys drifting into the river after major flooding.

Big Bend National Park in Texas. (National Park Service)

The federal government’s waiver authority to build border wall infrastructure was first applied in southern California, where it has caused devastating ecological and cultural damage. Two 30-foot-high prison-style walls now cut directly through Friendship Park, marring the binational landmark shared by San Diego and Tijuana that was established in 1971 as a symbol of solidarity and good will between the United States and Mexico.

The development of border barriers in the park has turned this vision of international kinship on its head.

“They’ve already destroyed the park”, says Dan Watman of Friends of International Friendship Park, an organization working to restore the site’s original mission and to protect Yogurt Canyon, which surrounds it.

Watman pointed to the first Trump administration’s use of a waiver to disregard the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, among other laws, to build wall barriers that destroyed habitat for the vulnerable burrowing owl.

“Today, there are no more burrowing owls left there,” he says.

Watman is deeply concerned that additional border wall construction in the park will continue to damage the canyon’s wildlife habitat and disrupt water flows.

He is also weary that the destruction of Friendship Park is just a preview of what the entire southern border will look like if the Trump administration continues down this path.

Dan Watman, with Friends of Friendship Park, speaks during a demonstration in front of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection – San Diego Border Patrol Sector Headquarters in 2022 in Chula Vista, California. (Nelvin C. Cepeda / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images)

For years, Earthjustice has worked successfully to protect border communities, wildlife, and public lands from the Trump administration’s reckless wall construction agenda.

When the first Trump administration declared a national emergency to justify building more miles of border wall in Texas, a move that would have destroyed a historic chapel and cemetery, we sued on behalf of the families whose loved ones were buried on the threatened site, successfully delaying the construction. The Biden administration ultimately withdrew the emergency declaration, saving the site.

We are now supporting a lawsuit filed by the Center for Biological Diversity to stop the Trump administration from using waivers to sidestep federal laws in its relentless push to construct border wall infrastructure in and around Big Bend National Park in Texas.

Disregarding vital environmental and public health regulations to build roads and other barriers here would have far-reaching, irreparable impacts on the park’s ecosystem and the local communities that have long relied on the economic and cultural benefits it provides.

In October, the district court took emergency action and blocked wall construction throughout the entire Big Bend region while the legal case continues.

This is a major victory, but our work is not over: The Trump administration has now asked the Supreme Court to intervene.

scraped.author: Abigail Dillen
scraped.h1: Voters Demanded Change – on the Environment, and Democracy
scraped.body_text:

Earthjustice serves hundreds of public-interest clients, providing top-tier legal representation free of charge — and we win. Because the earth needs a good lawyer.

Our Stories

Affordable clean energy, data center guardrails, and government accountability played out in midterm contests across the country.

By Abigail Dillen

On Tuesday, Americans voted for a change in direction – including on the environment.

Data centers were one major issue on the ballot. On Tuesday, data center bans or restrictions passed in at least 38 jurisdictions and counting across the country. In the states where the buildout is happening fastest, including Georgia, Ohio, and Texas, governors’ races turned on voter recognition of the need for stronger guardrails and robust community protections.

With rising power demand for data centers and rising energy costs, this election was also about the future of energy. Voters angry about growing energy bills focused attention on races for seats on the Georgia Public Service Commission, the body that regulates utilities in that state. Similar dynamics were seen in races for two seats on the Arizona Corporation Commission, another utility regulator, and one seat on the Texas Railroad Commission, which regulates the oil and gas industry.

These are small agencies with tremendous power. With these seats, there is an opportunity to usher in clean energy for people who are struggling with soaring energy costs. These were the opposite of sleepy races: Voters are understanding the connection between data centers, utility rates, and regulatory bodies.

And, in the midst of a rush to drill more oil and gas and entrench our fossil fuel dependence, voters rejected a ballot measure to establish a constitutional “right to gas” in Colorado, a major oil-and-gas-producing state. The oil and gas industry presented voters with a false choice between prosperity and policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Voters know better.

Among the most important debates in the country is how to build the infrastructure we need faster without running over people and wrecking the things we can’t afford to lose. For example, clean water and clean air. This “abundance” debate has its origins in the California housing crisis, and it has come to stand for the proposition that deregulation is the answer to our country’s problems. As data centers show what speed without guardrails looks like, the debate came full circle in California, with voters rejecting Prop 45, a sloppy effort to kill environmental review in the permitting process for even the most consequential projects.

This election is a thrilling reminder and a profound challenge: We can move forward together in this country if we are willing to throw in together, believe in our ambition for real change, and act on it.

Over the last two years, too many people have underestimated American voters and their ability to care about all the things that matter at once. This election was about the cost of living and an economy that must work infinitely better for everyone. It was also about our health, our health care, and the health of the communities where we live and work. It was about justice and the rights that Americans are not going to give up, no matter how much money is spent and how much power is abused to create division and drive despair.

People across this country did the real work to organize and vote. A whole bunch of courageous, good people stepped up to lead this work. The hope that millions of Americans felt on election night is a call to the most ambitious action. Let’s get to work!

We’ve received your feedback — thank you!

Fairplay, the nation’s leading nonprofit fighting to protect kids from the dangers of Big Tech and AI, released the following statement today in response to the Emma v. Google lawsuit .

Fairplay Associate General Counsel for AI and Privacy Brendan Bouffard said: “The idea of an untested AI chatbot helping a 13-year-old girl plan her own suicide should terrify all of us, but this is the sick new reality Google has created by forcing its AI products onto school-issued devices. Google claims its Chromebooks are there to help students learn, but in reality, the company was experimenting on kids like Emma by pushing them to use Gemini, a product the company knew was dangerous but rushed out anyway.

“We commend Emma’s parents and the EdTech Law Center for filing this urgent lawsuit. We also call on Congress and state legislatures to pass the People-First Chatbot Bill , model legislation we helped draft that will protect kids from AI harms.

“Let this be a reminder that ‘Google’ is not a verb. It’s the name of a surveillance and advertising company whose presence in schools has nothing to do with learning and everything to do with turning our kids into lifelong loyal customers.”

California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced today that he was moving to commute all death sentences in California, marking a historic step towards ending the death penalty in California and across the country.

The American Civil Liberties Union, ACLU of Southern California, ACLU of Northern California, ACLU of San Diego & Imperial Counties, and ACLU California Action joined the hundreds of organizations and individuals urging the Gov. Newsom to take this necessary step to address the persistent and systemic flaws with the death penalty in California.

Anthony D. Romero, executive director of the American Civil Liberties Union, issued the following statement:

“Today, Gov. Newsom made history by announcing his intention to commute every death sentence in California and clear the largest death row in the nation. In doing so, he honored his commitment to end a system that conflicts with human dignity, fairness, and the values enshrined in our Constitution.

“These commutations reflect what justice demands: an end to a racist, error-prone, and inhumane punishment that has burdened California for far too long. By taking this step, Gov. Newsom has affirmed that the death penalty has no place in California and he showed real courage by confronting racialized injustice head-on.

“The evidence against the death penalty has been overwhelming for decades. As the ACLU and allies have documented in courts across the country, a person’s risk of execution is predictable, but for all the wrong reasons: race, geography, and politics. Such profound, systemic injustice demands a systemic response. Today, California comes closer to closing the chapter on a cruel and morally and legally corrupt practice and sets a powerful example for others to follow.”

Gov. Newsom’s announcement comes amid ongoing legal challenges to California’s death penalty system. In April 2024, the ACLU, alongside the NAACP Legal Defense Fund and the Office of the State Public Defender, brought a lawsuit challenging the state’s death penalty statute as racially discriminatory and unconstitutional under the Equal Protection guarantees of the California Constitution.

The evidence presented in that lawsuit revealed pervasive racial bias in California’s implementation of the death penalty. Black people are up to eight times more likely to be sentenced to death when compared to similarly situated non-Black defendants, while Latino people are at least six times more likely to be sentenced to death.

Under California law, the governor has the unilateral authority to commute death sentences in cases without additional felony convictions. For cases involving additional felony convictions, the governor’s commutation request now goes to the California Supreme Court for review and approval.

Additional statements below are from ACLU affiliates in California:

Abdi Soltani, executive director of the ACLU of Northern California:

“The death penalty has no place in California – or any society that values justice, fairness, and human rights . Our organization has fought for decades against this antiquated, inhumane system, and we applaud the governor for taking bold action to end it.”

Chandra Bhatnagar, executive director of the ACLU of Southern California:

“From its inception, California has imposed the death penalty in a racially discriminatory manner, creating a two-tiered system of justice. With this historic act of clemency, the state can turn the page — rejecting a broken, biased system and embracing a more just and equitable future for all.”

Norma Chávez-Peterson, executive director of the ACLU of San Diego & Imperial Counties:

“Systemic injustices call for systemic solutions. By granting universal clemency to all people with death sentences in California, Governor Newsom has joined a chorus of leaders nationwide who have rejected the death penalty and recognized it as a failed and unjust experiment. This isn’t about individual cases, it is about addressing a system that is racist, fundamentally flawed, ineffective, and unfixable.”

Newly-elected Georgia governor Keisha Lance Bottoms

Well that was a night. The glad spectacle of a newly sentient America tottering back to its capacious ideals was dubbed Orange Crush, Bluenami, a political earthquake , a wily tweak to Hegseth's coveted public execution and "one of the great acts of defiance in American history." It was both landslide too big to rig or stop and "extinction-level" rout. Above all, it was a thunderous rejection of fear, greed, lies, cruelty, war-mongering, authoritarianism . Tell your kids, urged Abdul El-Sayed, "The bad guys lost."

Who knew, pundits marveled: Turns out if you keep lying, stealing, abusing children , terrorizing, kidnapping, assaulting neighbors, shooting people in the street, making it impossible to get food, gas, health care or education while gloating about it and lining your fat pockets, everyone hates you. So it was that a " Trump Reckoning " and GOP "Armageddon" beyond even their worst doomsday scenarios arrived wherein Democrats swept "nearly every race that matters” as Americans en masse embraced all the shithole, lunatic, transgender, anti-Semitic, dog-eating, Medicare-wanting Muslim Brotherhood communists they'd been so helpfully warned about, alas, in vain.

This, of course, despite MAGA's best/worst efforts to re-draw districts, shutter polling places, strong-arm election officials, browbeat brown and black voters, pre-litigate election results they couldn't buy, and launch 1,000 DOJ "polling monitors" into all 50 states in hopes of targeting vulnerable minority districts. And yet, noted Garrett Graff, nothing untoward happened. Instead, voters "gave America another chance." Millions stood up, showed up, voted early, refused to bend the knee or be silenced. Graff said a friend wrote from deep-red Mississippi, where Democrat Scott Colom still had a stunning, razor-thin lead. "My flabbers are gasted,” she wrote. “Be on the lookout for pigs in the sky."

"So much history was made last night," Graff added, much of it shaped by both the 250 years and then Trump's dark reign of white supremacist politics. The startling result: The most diverse set of newly elected lawmakers the country has ever seen, with one historian writing Dems are winning races "they haven’t won since they were the white supremacist party.” An Atlanta Journal-Constitution story begins, "In 1860, an enslaved man named Sheppard Peek was listed among the possessions of William Peek, a white man in Crawfordville"; Sheppard's value was placed at $1,400. In Georgia on Tuesday, his great-great-granddaughter, Keisha Lance Bottoms, was elected the first Black female governor in the country.

Bottoms is just one of many historic firsts . Xavier Becerra , the son of Mexican immigrants, became California's first elected Latino governor. Deb Haaland became New Mexico’s first Native governor. Wisconsin and Nevada elected their first Black governors. There are three other first women governors. New Hampshire's Chris Pappas will become the first out gay man in the Senate. scraped.title: Muslim, Jewish Groups Warn “Right to Worship” Bill Could Undermine Free Speech
scraped.description: “Protecting religious freedom must not come at the expense of other constitutional rights,” the groups explained.
scraped.author: Chris Walker
scraped.h1: Muslim, Jewish Groups Warn “Right to Worship” Bill Could Undermine Free Speech
scraped.body_text:
“Protecting religious freedom must not come at the expense of other constitutional rights,” the groups explained.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation .

Two religious organizations — one Jewish and one Muslim — are urging lawmakers to reject a bill that ostensibly aims to protect houses of worship but that would actually quell free speech rights.

“The Right to Worship Act,” sponsored by Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) and cosponsored by Republicans and Democrats alike, seeks to “protect” religious buildings and people inside them by limiting the First Amendment right to protest in nearby areas.

The bill prohibits activities within 100 feet of a house of worship that include actions that are “knowingly disrupting the scheduled religious service” or “impeding people from participating at [a] scheduled religious service.”

While the legislation limits protections to the period of time “beginning 1 hour before the start of and ending 1 hour after the conclusion of a scheduled religious service,” the ambiguous language of the bill could feasibly allow houses of worship to define almost any event as being “protected” from demonstrations happening nearby — for example, a church bake sale could be considered a “scheduled religious service” by some, as could a political event featuring a controversial speaker discussing religious topics.

“Offenders” could be fined $2,500 by the federal government for their first instance of violating the rules laid out in the bill, and up to $10,000 for subsequent violations. The bill also grants private individuals who feel that their religious rights have been violated the ability to sue for “damages” of up to $5,000 per violation.

While most sponsors of the bill are Republican, it does have bipartisan support. Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Michigan) has signed on as a cosponsor , and 13 Democrats are cosponsors of the House version of the bill .

The Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC) and Bend the Arc: Jewish Action issued a joint statement urging lawmakers to reject the legislation , arguing that it sacrifices protections for one fundamental liberty to provide unnecessary protections for another.

“As Muslim and Jewish organizations, we understand the urgent need to protect houses of worship from threats, violence, intimidation, and physical obstruction,” the statement from the two groups explained. “Every person deserves to practice their faith freely and safely. However, protecting religious freedom must not come at the expense of other constitutional rights.”

The organizations argued that the broad language of the bill risks “chilling lawful speech, peaceful assembly, and political protest, including on public sidewalks and streets.”

“The legislation fails to adequately distinguish between genuine threats to religious exercise and constitutionally protected expression,” they said, adding :

Our communities know firsthand the consequences of religious hatred and discrimination. We reject the notion that protecting Muslim and Jewish Americans requires weakening the constitutional freedoms that safeguard us all.

The groups are calling on other members of Congress to reject the bill, and in the future, for lawmakers to only “pursue narrowly tailored protections that safeguard religious communities without restricting lawful expression.”

The Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) has also condemned the bill , warning that it could limit speech protections for protests outside religious venues that are hosting Israeli settlement land sales, further promoting dispossession of Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

In an explainer on the legislation published in September, CAIR labeled the bill as essentially an “Illegal Israeli Settlements Protection Act” that, if enacted into law, could be used to “discourage lawful demonstrations against events promoting Palestinian dispossession.”

“Existing federal law already prohibits force, threats of force, and physical obstruction directed at religious worship,” the organization said in a statement . “CAIR therefore questions the need for a new civil-liability regime that could be used to burden constitutionally protected advocacy and dissent.”

“Hosting a political or commercial event in a religious building should not shield that activity from public accountability,” CAIR added.

Truthout is funded almost entirely by readers — that’s why we can speak truth to power and cut against the mainstream narrative. But independent journalists at Truthout face mounting political repression under Trump.

We rely on your support to survive McCarthyist censorship. Please make a tax-deductible one-time or monthly donation.

Focusing on both national and local topics since the early 2000s, he has produced thousands of articles analyzing the issues of the day and their impact on people. He can be found on most social media platforms under the handle @thatchriswalker .

scraped.title: CAIR Ends Operations in Florida as “Domestic Terrorist” Designation Takes Effect
scraped.description: Gov. Ron DeSantis has been attempting to put the Muslim civil rights organization out of business for nearly a year.
scraped.author: Mitch Perry
scraped.h1: CAIR Ends Operations in Florida as “Domestic Terrorist” Designation Takes Effect
scraped.body_text:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has been attempting to put the Muslim civil rights organization out of business for nearly a year.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Council on American Islamic Relations (CAIR) has suspended operations in Florida, the organization has announced .

It did so after a federal judge rejected an emergency request Wednesday by the Muslim civil rights organization to stop the state from designating the group and its state chapter as domestic terrorist organizations, allowing the designation to take effect while its legal challenge, litigated by the ACLU and the Southern Poverty Law Center, continues.

Federal Judge Allen C. Winsor of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida denied CAIR and CAIR Florida’s request to reverse the designation. In a ruling released Wednesday night, Windsor said the plaintiffs were unlikely to succeed at this stage on their claims that the designations under a new law ( HB 1471 ) violates their due process and First Amendment rights.

The judge did issue a narrow form of preliminary relief, stating that Florida prosecutors cannot enforce the law against CAIR and CAIR Florida, their employees, or third parties with respect to provision of legal services to the groups.

That designation took effect Thursday. As a result, both groups say they have been forced to shut down their advocacy and operations in Florida.

“Today’s ruling is deeply disappointing and we are appealing it,” said Ashley Gorski, senior counsel with the ACLU’s National Security Project.

“Today’s decision upholds state officials’ sweeping power to punish American organizations they brand as ‘terrorist,’ without due process and in violation of the First Amendment. Florida officials have been relentless in seeking to silence our clients’ civil rights work and advocacy, damaging not only them but also their community. We cannot allow this dangerous and sweeping censorship regime to stand.”

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and Attorney General James Uthmeier hailed the ruling Thursday. “Great win by our Solicitor General’s office and for the people of Florida!” Uthmeier wrote on X.

DeSantis and other members of the Florida Cabinet voted to designate CAIR and CAIR Florida as domestic terrorist organizations on Sept. 29. They contend the group operates as a front for Hamas and the Muslim Brotherhood.

Attorneys for CAIR have vehemently denied the allegation, contending its mission, “rooted in faith, is to enhance the public’s understanding of Islam, protect civil rights, promote justice and empower American Muslims.”

The designation in late September came months after DeSantis signed legislation approved by the Legislature earlier this year that gave five Florida executive officials — the head of domestic security (the commissioner of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement), the governor, and the three members of the state Cabinet — power to designate and eliminate groups operating in the United States without filing any legal charges or submitting their case to a jury.

The legislation prohibits any state agency, political subdivision, or public school district from expending or accepting state funds to support groups thus designated. It bans public schools or school districts from spending state or federal funds or maintaining programs on campus that “promote” a designated group.

The law also says any college or university must report information relating to the status of a student attending that school on a student visa if the student “promotes” a terrorist-designated organization. Students found to have promoted the group can be expelled.

The ACLU, the ACLU of Florida, and two other legal groups representing CAIR and CAIR Florida filed a lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of the legislation in July in the Northern District.

“As Florida chief of domestic security, I know there are imminent dangers to public health, safety, and welfare due to increasing risks from foreign and domestic terrorist groups,” then-FDLE Commissioner Mark Glass said on Sept. 11. Glass has since been replaced by Larry Keefe.

DeSantis has been attempting to put CAIR out of business for nearly a year. He issued an executive order in December designating CAIR and CAIR-Florida as terrorist organizations, directing state and local agencies to block them and their supporters from public contracts, funding, and benefits. After the groups sued, a federal judge issued a temporary injunction blocking the order in March.

Shortly afterwards, the Legislature passed and DeSantis signed HB 1471.

scraped.title: AIPAC Has Lost Over 30 of Its Midterm Races So Far, In Sign of Major Shift
scraped.description: Roughly two-thirds of the spending by the once insuperable lobbying group this cycle went toward races they lost.
scraped.author: Sharon Zhang
scraped.h1: AIPAC Has Lost Over 30 of Its Midterm Races So Far, In Sign of Major Shift
scraped.body_text:
Roughly two-thirds of the spending by the once insuperable lobbying group this cycle went toward races they lost.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) has lost dozens of races in which it backed a candidate in this year’s midterm elections, accounting for nearly two-thirds of the spending by the once insuperable political lobbying group, in a sign of its waning influence.

Politico found in a report on Thursday that more than 30 of the group’s candidates lost their elections this week. This marks “defeat for AIPAC in over three-fourths of the competitive races that have been called so far where it backed an incumbent,” Politico reported.

This includes candidates like Republican Representatives Mike Lawler (New York), Brian Fitzpatrick (Pennsylvania), and Max Miller (Ohio), as well as Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine), who fell to progressive Israel critic Troy Jackson, and Mike Rogers in Michigan.

Collins has been a staunch defender of Israel in the Senate, and AIPAC was her biggest outside donor by a massive margin during the race. AIPAC gave $2.8 million supporting her race against Jackson, as data from OpenSecrets showed ; the next-largest outside donor, investment firm KKR & Co., gave just a fraction of that, at $160,000.

AIPAC dumped even more money into the race against Michigan candidate Abdul El-Sayed, whose opposition to the U.S.-Israel relationship has been a hallmark of his campaign. AIPAC and its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), reportedly dropped up to $9 million supporting Rogers in the last weeks of the election. This came after AIPAC spent a whopping $30 million opposing El-Sayed and backing Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Michigan) in the primary.

The next largest target after El-Sayed was Daniel Biss, who won his election to the U.S. House in Illinois after UDP dumped $6.3 million against him. Biss explicitly ran on a platform opposing AIPAC and its influence.

These losses are staggering for a political group whose name was once synonymous with power in D.C. In fact, these results indicate that being affiliated with the group is becoming politically toxic, due in large part to the work of pro-Palestine advocates who spoke out against the group amid Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

AIPAC, perhaps concerned about losing donors, defended its record on X, arguing that it backed 245 candidates who won their races. But the contributions to these races represented only about a third of their spending in this cycle.

According to Responsible Statecraft , almost two-thirds of the money that AIPAC and UDP spent this cycle went toward losing candidates. Via UDP, AIPAC spent $84.1 million on elections — $55.3 million of which went toward races where their preferred candidate lost. This stands in sharp contrast to prior election cycles. In the 2022 midterm election, Responsible Statecraft found, 69 percent of UDP spending went toward races their candidate won. In 2024, their winning ratio was 87 percent.

AIPAC can still wield enormous power over Congress. In its first post-election post on social media on Wednesday, the lobbying group congratulated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) and Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-New York) for the “resounding victories for their caucuses.” The lawmakers are currently poised to lead the House and Senate when the new Congress begins in January, and are two of Israel’s staunchest defenders in Congress and major allies of AIPAC.

But the sands are quickly shifting under their feet. Opposing Israel and AIPAC have become increasingly normalized positions for politicians as the public overwhelmingly rejects the U.S.-Israel relationship, with even candidates in deep red states running against the lobbying group.

NEW poll: A supermajority of Jewish Americans believe Israeli & AIPAC actions increase antisemitism. 80% say Israel’s actions in Gaza & the West Bank increase antisemitism in the US. 66% say AIPAC’s campaign spending against candidates critical of Israel increases antisemitism. pic.twitter.com/oIS1wUYSRi

In Mississippi, for instance, Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom pledged to never take AIPAC money. He is currently holding on to a narrow lead over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Mississippi) in their election, and, if he wins, will be the first Democratic senator elected from the state since 1989.

“I will never take a penny from AIPAC or Super PACs that don’t put Mississippi and America first,” Colom said in a post on social media last month. “This Senate seat belongs to the people of Mississippi. That’s who I’ll answer to.”

scraped.title: Hell on earth: Stephen Miller is Trump's new chief of staff
scraped.description: The president makes it clear. The next two years will be war.
scraped.author: Inae Oh
scraped.h1: Hell on Earth: Stephen Miller Is Trump’s New Chief of Staff
scraped.body_text:
Mark Schiefelbein/AP

President Donald Trump is ending a bruising week of electoral humiliation with a clear message: He has no intention of changing tack. In fact, the president appears ready to double down on his worst instincts.

“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

That’s the singular message of Friday’s announcement that Trump is tapping Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, marking the alarming further rise of one of the administration’s most publicly reviled figures. The shake-up follows Tuesday’s Democratic sweep across the country, a rout widely viewed as a rejection of Trump and MAGA politics amid a deeply unpopular war and rising costs.

But perhaps most ominously, Miller’s ascension signals that Trump’s immigration crackdown will not slow down over the next two years unless Democrats find a way to break it with their new control of Congress. In selecting Miller, who is known for his aggressive, xenophobic rhetoric , Trump also replaces yet another prominent woman in his administration, following the firings of Kristi Noem, Pam Bondi, and Kimberly Guilfoyle.

“Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime. I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” Wiles posted on social media. “While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will.”

scraped.title: The Cybertruck is dead
scraped.description: Ugly, broken, and ultimately rejected, Tesla’s Cybertruck keeps tracing the MAGA trajectory.
scraped.author: Inae Oh
scraped.h1: The Cybertruck Is Dead
scraped.body_text:
Kotaro Numata/AP

After years of lagging sales and multiple high-profile recalls, Elon Musk announced on Friday that Tesla will start closing out production of the Cybertruck in 2027. The announcement marks the end of the road for a vehicle that became synonymous with the politics and aesthetics of MAGA: brutal, aggressive, and in-your-face .

“Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production,” Musk posted on X.

The announcement concludes a humiliating week for Musk , after spending $445 million backing Republicans ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections only for Democrats to seize control of Congress in dozens of history-making elections around the country. The blue wave was especially felt in Texas , where, in recent years, Musk moved significant portions of his business in order to avoid regulation and oversight by Democrats in California. It was during this relocation that the Cybertruck, which debuted in 2023, quickly became linked to Musk’s politics, and later, his singular role in destroying much of the federal government.

But the Cybertruck was plagued with serious problems that went well beyond its association with Musk’s MAGA embrace. Its obnoxious, hulking steel design—which included bulletproof windows that many saw as emblematic of the right’s crime panic—was roundly mocked; multiple recalls were announced; and sales repeatedly struggled.

In other words, ugly, broken, and ultimately rejected. Even in the end, the Cybertruck traces a familiar MAGA trajectory.

items.summary: Americans overwhelmingly despise President Donald Trump’s proposed 250-foot high “triumphal arch.” More than 100,000 people submitted written comments to the Interior Department, most opposing its placement near the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. With its “eternal flame,” the golden winged figure on top, and now possibly snipers and a munitions dump for its alleged “national […] Americans overwhelmingly despise President Donald Trump’s proposed 250-foot high “triumphal arch.” More t...

scraped.title: Trump’s triumphal arch hits a blue wall
scraped.description: Even private money won’t save the project, Rep. Don Beyer says, if lawmakers ban it in the budget.
scraped.author: Stephanie Mencimer
scraped.h1: Trump’s Triumphal Arch Hits a Blue Wall
scraped.body_text:
A replica of President Trump's proposed triumphal arch at the Great American State Fair on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. on July 1, 2026. Francis Chung/POLITICO via AP Images

Americans overwhelmingly despise President Donald Trump’s proposed 250-foot high “triumphal arch.” More than 100,000 people submitted written comments to the Interior Department, most opposing its placement near the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. With its “eternal flame,” the golden winged figure on top, and now possibly snipers and a munitions dump for its alleged “national security” importance, the arch has even been compared to Nazi monuments .

No matter. Trump had threatened to begin construction on the arch as soon as the now Trump-aligned National Capital Planning Commission held its final vote approving it, which it did late Thursday night. His hand-picked majority said the digging should start, and almost immediately after the decision, US District Court Judge Tanya S. Chutkan said the digging should stop.

She had previously instructed the administration to notify her within 30 minutes of any construction activity after the vote, having learned from Trump’s previous moves that he was inclined to start construction before the courts could act. Her ruling, in a lawsuit filed by veterans horrified by the monstrous size of the monument and its impact on nearby Arlington National Cemetery, put a 14-day moratorium on the project.

On Friday morning, the White House did not seem particularly concerned about the delay by what White House spokesman Davis Ingle called the “activist district court.” In an email to Mother Jones , he said, “We are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds and look forward to seeing the completion of this magnificent Arch—a tribute to 250 years of American greatness.”

Even if Trump eventually does prevail in court, Democrats who won control of both the House and Senate Tuesday by large margins intend to ensure that the only arch constructed in Memorial Circle is the fake one put up by protesters Thursday.

Big day for a decision on the Arc de Trump. Lots of protesters out: pic.twitter.com/LuCJMEPoBT

At that protest, I spoke with Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.), whose district includes Arlington Cemetery. While I was tempted to ask him about buying a new Volvo—the congressman is a well-known Northern Virginia car dealer—I asked him if the new Congress would be able stop to the unpopular Trump monument. “Congress has to give permission before it can be built,” Beyer assured me.

Of course, lack of approval hasn’t stopped Trump from moving forward with other projects before, such as mowing down trees at East Potomac Park for his planned golf course, or tearing down the East Wing to build a ballroom.

Trump has tried to give the arch plan the patina of official approval through the NCPC vote. But after he stacked the commission with his allies, the outcome of its Thursday vote was never in doubt, despite the fact that at least 130 people had signed up to testify, mostly against the project.

The NCPC Chairman Mark Paoletta made it clear their testimony was purely performative. “As chairman of the National Capital Planning Commission,” he wrote in an October op-ed in The Federalist , “I applaud President Trump’s historic efforts to build a monumental arch at Memorial Circle, and will vote to approve this project.” The NCPC did so with a vote of 8 to 4.

That’s why, Beyer said, he had been concerned about “how much construction will happen before January” before the new Congress is sworn in. While he believes Congress can eventually stop the arch, Beyer says, “We’re counting on the judge in the short run.”

“Even if he raises the money privately, we can put specific language in the budget that prohibits the construction of the arch on this federal land.”

Once Democrats regain control of Congress, he says they have legislation sure to pass both houses that he knows Trump “won’t sign.” But he says Congress can and will use its budget authority to check Trump’s power. Trump seems to be anticipating this move. On Friday morning, the White House promoted a new website on its social media channels showing its grand plans for the arch.

A Monument to the American Spirit. The Military Triumphal Arch will honor the heroes who gave everything for our nation – a monumental tribute to America’s first 250 years & a symbol of the next 250. A legacy of freedom. A future without limits. 📲 https://t.co/vkquwA5qGp pic.twitter.com/ucUPdw3YLL

The website indicates that it’s the product of the United States Triumphal Arch Foundation, whose chairman is Randy Evans, a Georgia Republican who served as ambassador to Luxembourg in Trump’s first term. The White House did not respond to follow up questions about the foundation. But the setup suggests Trump plans to seek private financing to circumvent Congress and complete the arch, just as he has done for his other pet project, the White House ballroom.

Beyer says Congress is not going to let that happen. “Even if he raises the money privately,” Beyer said, “we can put specific language in the budget that prohibits the construction of the arch on this federal land.”

Tuesday’s historic blue wave election has also given Democrats new avenues for putting constraints on the Builder-in-Chief. In January, Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) will become the chair of the House Committee on Natural Resources, which oversees the Interior Department, the agency currently pushing the arch. He testified at the NCPC meeting on Thursday and was very clear about the direction the new Democratic Congress planned to go. “We are a nation of laws,” Huffman said, “not kings or kangaroo commissions.”

He issued a stern warning to contractors and government employees who might be considering executing Trump’s orders to start construction. Contractors have already started to mark up the site, even though it hasn’t been approved yet. “This arch is illegal,” Huffman said, ticking off the list of federal statutes it violates. And because Congress has not authorized its construction, he suggested that anyone advancing it “will put themselves at legal risk…Because in case you hadn’t heard, we’ll soon have a new Congress that takes the rule of law very seriously.”

BRAVO 🔥: “We’re a nation of laws, not kings or kangaroo commissions.” Rep. Jared Huffman said that to the commission’s face at the hearing on Trump’s arch. Watch at 0:36 when he reminds them who they pledged allegiance to, then tells them to reject the damn thing. pic.twitter.com/WZbByxJSg5
